name: Capillaria philippinensis

taxonomy.rank_note: Reference groups can include multiple species. Protozoan higher-rank systems differ; the lineage is provided without forcing every clade into a class rank.

morphology: Egg: approximately 35–45 × 20–25 µm, peanut-like with striated shell and relatively flattened bipolar plugs.
Eggs, larvae and adults can appear in stool; internal autoinfection can increase burden.

transmission.detail: Humans acquire larvae in raw or inadequately cooked small fish; intestinal adults produce eggs and larvae, with possible autoinfection.

life_cycle.detail: Humans acquire larvae in raw or inadequately cooked small fish; intestinal adults produce eggs and larvae, with possible autoinfection.
Eggs, larvae or adult fragments in stool.

hosts: Definitive: humans and probably fish-eating birds in the natural cycle. Intermediate: fish.
distribution: Reported particularly in the Philippines and Thailand, with other regional cases.
clinical_significance: Chronic watery diarrhea, weight loss, protein-losing enteropathy and electrolyte disturbance can become severe.
specimen: Eggs, larvae or adult fragments in stool.
diagnostics: Repeated stool microscopy may be required; 400× helps resolve striations and polar plugs.
differential_diagnosis: Compare with larger smooth-shelled Trichuris eggs with more prominent plugs; do not depend on shape without scale.
review_status: Source-compiled educational content; not independently clinically validated
description: Capillaria philippinensis — Intestinal capillary worm. Chronic watery diarrhea, weight loss, protein-losing enteropathy and electrolyte disturbance can become severe.

annotation_guidance: Record specimen, stage, stain, objective/total magnification, pixel calibration, source image and reviewer certainty.
Native crops of 200–650 pixels do not determine biological size. Retain µm-per-pixel calibration before resizing.
Split training, validation and test data by patient/specimen; keep related crops in the same split.
Keep damaged or ambiguous objects uncertain. Molecular confirmation of a mixed specimen does not assign every pictured object a species.
